Garfield Sobers, born in Bridgetown in 1936, is widely seen as the greatest all-round cricketer ever: a great batsman, a bowler of three styles and a fine fielder. He played for the West Indies from 1954 to 1974.

In 1958, at 21, he scored 365 not out against Pakistan, a Test record that stood for 36 years until Brian Lara passed it. In 1968 he became the first man to hit six sixes in an over in first-class cricket.

He captained the West Indies and was knighted in 1975. Barbados made him a National Hero. His success showed what Caribbean players could do in the colonial game, as Viv Richards did after him.
